source: ACIAR Monograph No. 146a, "ដំណាំសំណែកសៀង" [Soybean Growers Manual], Belfield S., Brown C., Martin M. (eds.), New South Wales Department of Primary Industries / Murdoch University / CARDI / ACIAR, 2012
text:
This is one of the manual's most detailed chapters. It covers all major and micronutrients relevant to soybean:

Nitrogen (N): soybean's own biological nitrogen fixation via Bradyrhizobium root nodules can supply much of its N requirement once nodulation is well established, but the manual cautions that nodulation takes time to become fully effective and a modest starter N application at planting can help young plants before nodules are active; over-application of N fertilizer is warned against because it can suppress nodulation.

Phosphorus (P) and Potassium (K): the manual explains P's role in root and nodule development and flowering, and K's role in overall plant vigour and stress tolerance, with recommended source fertilizers — DAP (diammonium phosphate), MAP (monoammonium phosphate), single/triple superphosphate for P; muriate of potash (KCl) and sulfate of potash for K — presented in a nutrient-content comparison table (a table of common fertilizer products giving their %N, %P₂O₅, %K₂O, and %S content: urea 46:0:0; DAP 18:46:0; MAP 12:61:0; and several NPK+S blend products).

Sulfur (S): discussed as often under-supplied in Cambodian soils and needed at meaningful rates, with gypsum and sulfate-form fertilizers (e.g. sulfate of potash, single superphosphate) noted as good S sources.

Micronutrients: molybdenum (Mo) is highlighted as directly required for the nitrogen-fixation enzyme (nitrogenase) in the root nodules — a Mo deficiency can look like an N deficiency because it cripples nodule function; zinc (Zn) is discussed for its role in enzyme systems and is noted as more likely to be deficient on sandy soils; other micronutrients (boron, iron, manganese, copper) are mentioned more briefly with symptom notes.

Soil pH management: liming acid soils is recommended to correct pH into the range soybean and its rhizobia both tolerate well (the manual explains that overly acid soil both directly stresses the plant and reduces nodule Rhizobium survival/activity), with dolomitic lime specifically recommended where both Ca and Mg are needed.
